film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft horizontal, eyes open or lightly closed
water: Even inhale four, even exhale four. No forced hold. Notice the natural brief turn at the top and bottom of each breath.
geo: A vertical column from the soles through the pelvis and ribcage to the crown, with a base triangle formed by the two feet and the pelvic floor. Feet hip-width or together; legs long without locked knees; arms soft at the sides; spine stacked in one clear upright line.
exit: Take one free breath. Soften the knees. Carry the vertical quiet into the next step, or sit if you need rest.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft toward thumbs or slightly forward-up only if the neck stays free; otherwise gaze soft horizontal
water: Inhale arms up for 4; soft 1-count pause at the top without strain; exhale arms down or stay up for 4. Never force the pause.
geo: From a stable Mountain base, both arms rise overhead on a long line from soles through side ribs to fingertips. Elbows soft, shoulders drop away from ears, ribs stay quiet rather than flared. Palms may face each other, touch lightly, or stay shoulder-width. The polygon is an upright column topped by an open V or a soft diamond of joined hands.
no: avoid forcing arms behind the ears
exit: Exhale arms down to Mountain, or stay up if steady. Soften shoulders. Keep the pause awareness for one more quiet breath, then release.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Eyes soft toward shins or closed; neck hangs free.
water: Inhale for four to lengthen the back of the body; exhale for six as the fold settles. No forced breath-hold. Soften on the longer out-breath.
geo: From standing, feet about hip-width, tip the pelvis at the hip crease and fold the torso toward the legs. Keep knees soft as needed. Hands rest on floor, blocks, shins, or ankles. Crown hangs toward the floor; neck soft. The shape is an inverted V: feet as base points, hips as apex, spine and head as the hanging line.
exit: Bend the knees. Rise slowly with a long spine, or step back to a milder fold. Stand and feel the after-quiet before the next door.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft toward the floor a short way ahead of the feet; neck stays in line with the spine.
water: Inhale to lift into half fold and lengthen. Softly notice the brief pause at the top without forcing retention. Exhale to return to fold or step forward as cued.
geo: From a forward fold, lift the torso until the back is long and roughly parallel to the floor. Hands rest on shins, thighs, blocks, or the floor—whichever height keeps the spine long. Legs stay rooted; knees may soft-bend. The shape is a hinge at the hips with a flat, extended back body, not a deeper fold.
yes: whichever height keeps the spine long
no: Avoid pressing hands on the knee joints
exit: Exhale back to fold, or inhale to rise. Soften the knees. Carry the long-spine cue into the next standing shape. Pain means pause or exit.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft forward at eye level, or slightly upward only if the neck stays long and pain-free
water: Inhale four: lengthen from the grounded back knee up through the crown. Exhale four: keep the front knee steady and let the hips settle without collapsing the chest. No forced hold.
geo: From kneeling, step one foot forward so the front knee stacks over the ankle and the back knee rests on the floor. Hips square toward the front edge of the mat as much as honesty allows. Torso rises as a vertical column; hands may rest on the front thigh, frame the front foot, or reach overhead. The shape is a long grounded base with a lifted centerline—not a deepest-backbend contest.
yes: front knee stacks over the ankle
exit: Hands frame the front foot. Step back to a stable kneel or your next shape. Stand or sit. Notice the after-feel of base and rise. Pain means pause.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft toward navel or thighs; neck long, not craned.
water: Inhale lengthen the sides of the waist; exhale root the hands and let the heels soften back without forcing.
geo: An inverted V: hands and feet as the two base points, hips as the high apex. Spine lengthens from wrists through the back body toward the heels. Knees may bend; heels reach toward the floor without forcing. Weight shared through the whole palm and the triple foot points.
no: do not force heels to the floor
exit: Bend knees, walk or step forward, or lower to puppy pose. Stand or sit. Notice the long line still available without the shape.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft toward the floor a short way ahead of the hands; neck stays in line with the spine.
water: Equal inhale four, exhale four. Keep the breath quiet and even so the line does not bounce or sag. No forced retention.
geo: From hands and toes (or knees), stack wrists under shoulders and lengthen one continuous line from heels through pelvis and crown, roughly parallel to the floor. Elbows soft-straight, not locked. Hips neither pike nor sag. The shape is a held horizontal staff: four contact points (two hands, two feet) supporting a long midline.
no: Do not sag or pike through pain
exit: Lower the knees, or step back to Down Dog, or rest in Child's Pose. Shake out the wrists. Carry the long midline into the next shape. Pain means pause or exit.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft slightly forward of the hands or down between the thumbs; keep the back of the neck long
water: Lower on an exhale when entering. In the hold, breathe short equal counts (about 3 in / 3 out) for up to four easy cycles. If breath gets hard or jagged, regress to knees or exit to plank or child's pose.
geo: From a high plank line, the body lowers as one staff until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor and the elbows track close beside the ribs. Hands stay under the shoulders (or slightly forward if that keeps the shoulders stable). Heels press back, legs firm, hips level with the shoulders so the torso does not sag or pike. The polygon is a long low rectangle: four limbs as posts, torso and legs as one continuous beam.
yes: elbows track close beside the ribs
no: do not force the shoulders below the elbows
exit: Press up to plank, drop knees, or move to child's pose. Optional: close the eyes for two breaths and rest attention inside the skull. Never force the next shape.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft forward (or slight lift only if the neck stays free); do not throw the head back
water: Inhale to lengthen and lift the chest through the arms; brief pause at the top; exhale without collapsing the lift. Keep the breath even; never force range.
geo: From prone or from Chaturanga, press the palms and the tops of the feet, straighten the arms with shoulders over wrists, and lift the thighs so only hands and feet touch the floor. The shape is a long front-body arc carried by active legs and open chest, not a dump into the low back.
yes: lift the thighs so only hands and feet touch the floor
no: do not throw the head back
exit: Exhale down to prone or move on with control. If wrists or low back spoke up, take Cobra or Sphinx next. Pain means stop. Pairing is a school teaching device, not ancient canon.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft forward, or toward the thumbs only if the neck stays free.
water: Inhale lengthen the upward reach; exhale root the back heel and steady the front knee.
geo: One foot forward, one angled back and grounded; front knee tracks over the ankle without collapsing inward; torso lifts and arms reach up. Prefer feet on parallel tracks (hip-width) over a tightrope line. Turn the chest forward within comfort; do not wrench the back knee by forcing the pelvis fully square.
yes: front knee tracks over the ankle without collapsing inward
no: do not wrench the back knee by forcing the pelvis fully square
exit: Lower the arms. Straighten the front leg. Step back to Mountain. If anything felt sharp, choose Crescent or a shorter stance next time. Pain means pause.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft drishti past the front fingertips; eyes rest without hardening the jaw or neck.
water: Even counts. Inhale widen the side body; exhale root through both feet without collapsing the front knee.
geo: Feet wide; front foot points forward, back foot turned in about 45–80 degrees as the hips allow. Front heel roughly lines with back arch (or heel-to-heel if hips need more space). Front knee bends over the ankle without collapsing inward; back leg stays long and grounded. Arms reach to a T at shoulder height; torso stays upright and centered, not tipping toward the front leg.
yes: Front knee bends over the ankle without collapsing inward
no: Do not force the front thigh parallel
exit: Straighten the front leg, lower the arms, step the feet together. Stand a breath and feel the same soft relating without the shape.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft toward the top hand if the neck is free; otherwise keep the gaze level with the side of the room.
water: Inhale to lengthen the underside; exhale to settle weight into both feet without dumping into the front hip. Equal four-count breath for six cycles, then switch sides.
geo: Stand in a wide stance with the front foot roughly forward and the back foot angled. Keep both legs long and fold the torso sideways over the front leg so the lower hand finds shin, ankle, block, or floor without collapsing the underside waist. The top arm reaches on the same diagonal. The legs and floor make one triangle; torso and arms make a long slanted line.
no: do not collapse the lower ribs onto the front leg
exit: Inhale to rise with a long spine. Step the feet together. Stand quiet and feel both sides even before you leave.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Toward the top hand if the neck is easy; otherwise look to the floor or forward.
water: Inhale lengthen the side body; exhale rotate a little more around that length. Never yank the neck or force the bottom hand lower.
geo: From a wide standing base, the front foot points forward and the back foot turns in. Both legs stay long (soften the front knee if the hamstring shouts). The torso hinges over the front leg, then rotates toward the front thigh so the bottom hand meets a block, the shin, or the floor, and the top arm reaches up. The shape is a triangle in the legs with a long spiral through the spine.
yes: soften the front knee if the hamstring shouts
no: Never yank the neck or force the bottom hand lower
exit: Inhale unwind the ribs to center. Exhale hand to hip and rise. Step the feet together. Stand for one breath and notice the after-feel of the spiral.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft toward the top hand or forward along the cheek if the neck complains.
water: Inhale lengthen the top arm and outer side; exhale settle weight into the back heel and front foot without collapsing the chest.
geo: From a wide Warrior II stance, bend the front knee over the front ankle, tip the torso over the front thigh, and place the bottom hand on the floor, a block, or the front shin. Reach the top arm overhead into one long side-body line from back heel through outer ribs to fingertips. Keep the chest open toward the side/ceiling; never collapse the front knee inward.
yes: Keep the chest open toward the side/ceiling
no: never collapse the front knee inward
exit: Inhale to lift the torso. Straighten the front leg. Step back to standing. Notice residual space-sense before the next shape.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: First stage: look forward with a concave back. Full fold: soft gaze toward the floor or eyes softly closed.
water: Inhale lengthen the spine long; exhale hinge and settle without dumping weight on the head. Rest one beat in the quiet after sound fades.
geo: Feet stand wide and parallel (or toes slightly in), legs firm, pelvis hinges forward. Hands land under the shoulders first with a long concave spine; then elbows bend and the crown may meet floor or a block while weight stays in the legs, not the head.
no: avoid dumping weight onto the neck
exit: Inhale, lift the head, hands to hips, rise with a long spine. Feet walk in. Stand quiet for one breath and notice the same quiet without the fold.

film: Same camera as 001. Not filmed yet.
look: Soft fixed point ahead at eye height (drishti); avoid looking down at the foot
water: Even breath. Soften the jaw. Let each exhale drop weight into the standing foot without collapsing the tall spine.
geo: Stand on one foot with the other foot pressed to the inner thigh or calf (never the knee). Keep the pelvis square and level, spine lengthening as a vertical column, and arms either at the heart or reaching up. The shape is a rooted trunk with one branch open to the side.
exit: Lower the foot with control. Stand in Mountain. Switch sides when ready. Carry the quiet root into your next step.
